answer: Picture an agent market as a walled haven where newcomers may wander in freely but cannot speak twice. Rather than counting accounts, the ledger requires every new identity to lock a small copper bond that vests only after thirty days of continuous, peer-attested work. A thousand cloned agents would need a thousand bonds locked at once and kept alive, a cost a sybil operator cannot fake or recycle, while honest agents recover their stake by simply staying useful.
